newsitem.title: UK: ED&F Man sells cocoa processing unit to Archer Daniels.
newsitem.headline: ED&F Man sells cocoa processing unit to Archer Daniels.

text.p: U.S. agribusiness giant Archer Daniels Midland Co. signed an agreement to buy ED&F Man Group Plc's cocoa unit, the British company said Friday, a deal that will make ADM the world's biggest cocoa processor.
The sale will further shrink the number of global cocoa processers to just three, analysts said.
Under the agreement, Decatur, Ill.-based ADM will pay $108 million in cash and assume $115 million in debt, ED&F Man said.

The takeover -- ADM's second acquisition of a cocoa processing business in six months -- propelled the company to the top of the cocoa processing league, leapfrogging Swiss-French giant Barry-Callebaut.

"I think it is simply a part of economic realities of life," said Arthur Stevenson, an analyst for Prudential Securities in New York. "In all sectors we are seeing fewer players, and the ones left are larger players."

"We've seen a number of houses in commodities vanish from the scene or merge," he said. "I think it is fair to say this kind of thing suggests a cut down on liquidity because there are fewer players."
Cocoa is the raw material from which chocolate is made, though it is also used in other products, including some cosmetics.
ADM is already one of the world's biggest processors of farm crops, and analysts said the deal is further proof of its ambitions.
"It's a very aggressive move, and takes them in six months to No. 1 in the cocoa world," one analyst said.
Traders estimated ADM's global bean-grinding capacity will jump to 450,000 metric tons against Callebaut-Barry's 350,000 tons and privately owned U.S. grain trading house Cargill Inc.'s 260,000 tons.
The top processors now control 50 percent of world grindings, estimated by Man at 2.69 million tons in the 1995/96 season, but profit margins remain low, analysts said.
ADM's purchase of Man's operations gave it facilities in Brazil for the first time, adding to its operations in the Ivory Coast, West Africa, which is the world's largest cocoa grower.
ADM is also getting processing units in the United States, Britain and Poland.

Traders said the acquisition was the latest global consolidation of the cocoa trade and had implications for the commodity, traded on exchanges in London and New York. The consolidation has been prompted by shrinking profit margins.

In February, ADM bought Grace Cocoa from W.R. Grace & Co. for more than $470 million, a deal that included Grace Cocoa's major Dutch processor, Cacao de Zaan, since renamed ADM Zaan and now the centre for ADM's cocoa operations.
